rows.what the ink shows: The initial R has a closed upper loop; the two p descenders and the separate tall l of la survive the strike. In the last word the opening c, intermediate tall crossed strokes and the final tion sequence remain visible beneath the continuous cancellation.

A looped descending shaft and two dotted uprights survive above propres, but the heavy horizontal deletion merges the middle bodies and word divisions. The surviving strokes do not recover the three-word insertion.
There is a distinct initial upright-and-return d before the e/c group, followed by a dotted i and a tall crossed t near the end. The initial d rules out croissants.
The first group has a rounded e and tall crossed t; to its right the l rises above the compressed e/s group. The sloping deletion crosses these bodies without erasing their principal strokes.

The beginning has a tall l-like loop and separate raised dot, followed by a low looped group; farther right a g-like descender and narrow rising loop remain. The joined endings do not securely establish the proposed word divisions range les.
A tall initial f-like shaft and the following i dot are visible. The rest is a long compressed baseline, so the internal ie and final s cannot be counted securely.

The first short group is heavily compressed, and the following g-like descender leads into a long joined body whose middle uprights are not separable. The final même has the paired m shoulders and terminal e curl.

Four groups are visible: an initial a-loop, partir with a p descender, crossed upright and i-dot, then du and rang with a terminal g return. The initial accent is inseparable from the descenders of the inserted line above, so only à/a remains uncertain.
The initial on is separate from the next group; joint has the dotted descending j, a second raised dot and the tall final crossed t. The intervening low joins are visible.

A separate comma is followed by an elongated low continuation stroke with several darker points. There is no tall l or a separable es body; the unit is punctuation and a continuation mark rather than les.

There is one baseline lambda with a separate lower-right n, followed by a curved opening parenthesis and one baseline u. The crowded terminal strokes form the closing-parenthesis region; there is no superscript or second baseline lambda in this unit.

The next unit begins with a tall l-shaped loop and continues in a low horizontal tail, which can represent compressed es. The tail does not preserve separate letter bodies; the source termes is not supported.
The final word has a down-and-up initial stroke, a detached dark spot and an elongated low tail. No secure l or nuls sequence is visible, so this unit remains one unreadable word.
A tall red upright follows the question mark, with a tapered lower continuation. No detached lower dot is visible, so an exclamation mark cannot be securely distinguished from a marginal stroke.

The crossed rho retains its upper loop and descending stem; the low index is a short upright, like the clear 1 directly below. The horizontal return farther right belongs to the opening parenthesis; no broad n shoulder is visible.

The lambda has its tall slant and two lower legs. Its separate low index is a single short downstroke, matching the boxed lambda_1 below rather than the long horizontal n elsewhere on this page; the u and closing parenthesis survive.
Beneath the cancelled sup there is a small crossed x, a rounded membership sign whose middle merges with the strike, and an F with upright and two right bars.
Two separate left norm bars precede a tall h stem and low shoulder; F sits distinctly below it. Two right strokes remain at the closing norm bars despite the diagonal cancellation.

The raised group contains an upper loop crossed by the enclosing line, a diagonal descending left, and a heavy lower hooked glyph. The overlap prevents a secure separation of the proposed numerator 1 and denominator 2.
A tall h ascender falls into a low shoulder, and a separate F with vertical stem and two bars sits below and to its right. The horizontal deletion crosses h without hiding those shapes.
Black and red strike strokes cover the connected word bodies. A raised loop, two short uprights and dots remain, but they do not establish the complete les espaces sequence.
The subscript to the right of E has a small loop and a flattened rightward tail. The cancellation crosses the shoulder, leaving insufficient separation to establish n.

The first group has a curved upright ending in a short foot; the next begins with a tall returning stem and a long low body. The cross-out covers the intervening letter bodies, so la forme remains uncertain.

The word is reduced to a short initial cup, a long rising stroke, then a separated low run with two small humps and a terminal hook. No distinct t crossbar or i dot establishes the full vectoriels sequence.

The cancelled word preserves an initial curved body, a long descending stroke, a later upright and two separated dots. The horizontal deletion merges the connecting bodies, so the proposed contribution cannot be read throughout.

After the single baseline h is one compact raised mark with a pointed upper arm, closed dark loop and lower-right lobe. It differs from the separate outer 2 with curved top and flat foot and from the open angular 2 on the following h; no second baseline letter is present.
The capital E has an upright and three rightward bars. Its low following index is overrun by zigzag cancellation, so the n cannot be isolated securely.

A compact raised residue remains after the final norm, with a short descending/slanted return. The thick cancellation also crosses the preceding index and conceals the upper curve and foot needed to identify 2.
Two heavy horizontal swipes and rising diagonals cover the word body; a curved left return and one central ascender survive, but no complete letter sequence can be separated.
The ending l-u-t survives as an upright, a broad lower return and a terminal cross-stem. The preceding en conc bodies are fused into the thick horizontal strike.

The initial E has a detached upper stroke, followed by the low connected n; the next word begins with a descending p and retains compact rounded and horizontal strokes through osant before the large deletion loop.

One sum-shaped glyph, one baseline rho and a following u remain at left, and the two equals strokes remain separate. Large looping cancellation masks the grouping and raised powers, and crosses parts of the right norm and its index.

The initial tall L and small connected es traces remain, followed by a d ascender and a separate tall stem at the third word. The long deletion line swallows the middle bodies needed to establish deux théorèmes.
A tall T-like upright and short hooked fragments extend above and below two crossing strokes. The following letter bodies are merged into the cancellation and cannot be segmented.
The first letter has a straight ascender and a small rounded shoulder at its foot, the minuscule k form. The following y descends well below it; F has two separate rightward arms.

The final separator has a short horizontal body with a downward projection at its right edge, but no separate vertical crossing can be traced. The neighboring n+1 comparator has a clearer central cross, so this compressed sign remains plus/minus uncertain.

The final separator has a horizontal arm, an upward right tip and a lower spur; those tips cannot be traced as one vertical crossing. The preceding n arch and following upright 1 are separate and secure, leaving only this sign uncertain.
Two arms meet at a leftward point. There is blank paper immediately below them, with no separate lower equality bar; the distant horizontal line is the surrounding box.
